chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man for whom I want to establish a buy-back deal with wealth, and there is already some wealth of mine upon him before that. So he asks me for wealth, increasing the wealth that is already mine upon him. Would it be correct if I were to increase the wealth and sell him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, saying: 'I sell you this pearl for one thousand dirhams on the condition that I defer your payment of its price and my wealth upon you, such and such months.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.أُعَيِّنَهُ: to establish/fix a specific deal or buy-back

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell an item at a higher price and defer payment to offset an existing debt in Islamic finance?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the permissibility of 'bai' al-mu'ayyanah' (buy-back), where a creditor sells an item to a debtor at an inflated price while deferring payment to offset an existing debt. The scholar's response 'la ba'sa' confirms that this specific mechanism, often used to manage liquidity or consolidate debts, is valid in Shia jurisprudence provided the transaction elements are distinct. It highlights the flexibility in commercial contracts to accommodate practical financial needs without violating core principles of sale and debt.
